title: Playing heavy, soft-touch bassists and plywood basses
summary: He says he plays loud and heavy, names soft players who use amplifiers, and compares carved wood basses with plywood ones.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Is it a bigger tone? Do you have to work harder? Does it mean working easier on it so you don't have to work so hard to get a big tone?
Well, I actually work hard. I just, I mean, I always did play a heavy bass. Always did. I don't say I always played exactly right, but I always did play loud and real heavy.
You think most of the New Orleans fellas played pretty heavy, would you say?

Well, no, we have quite a few of them that play soft bass. I mean, you take, for instance, McClane. I think he's got a soft touch. He's a nice bass player, a real nice bass, but he's, he plays a soft bass. I think he's got an amplifier now. An amplifier would help him. I don't think he uses it in the paddock. No. But he's a, he's a fine bass man, but he's a very soft man. Rick Hart plays soft too most of the time. He, he carries an amplifier. Yeah. But I just don't like the, the amplified bass. I don't care too much for the fender. But, uh, if Dixon Land music don't pick up for me, as soon as I can go to rock and roll, I have to get a fender, because that's all they want now.

What about the laminated wood? You mentioned that once. Do you think that, can you tell the difference between the old style construction, carved out of one big thick piece of wood, they start the big thing four or five inches thick when they make them right?

Oh, there's a different tonation there. That's the, real tone itself, that wood. I mean, of course, the thing I got, I mean, is the plywood bass. I mean, just my heavy playing, I guess, that brings up the tone the way it did. But I mean, uh, it sounds good to me. Well, it's natural wood bass. I mean, uh, nice. The same as a guitar. I mean, you got a guitar, one of them old guitars that's a natural wood. You got a beautiful instrument, a beautiful sounding instrument. But you get those, uh, these modern guitars, they all plywood with, uh, all this mechanism. Oh, wash bone. Yeah. I mean, anything. They make them out of compressed paper, I guess, most of the time. Wash bone. Good dread wood. Wash bone. Well, that's just a block in here from compressed paper.
